target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S Fm] (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓢]
    (T D : Fm → Fm) (σ G : Fm),
    Def11 𝓢 D T → 𝓢 ⊢ D σ → 𝓢 ⊢ D G → 𝓢 ⊢ D (σ 🡒 G)
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is defined to be the following proposition. For every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of implication, conjunction, disjunction, negation, truth and falsehood on Fm, every provability relation for S on Fm, every system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens, every pair of functions T, D from Fm to Fm, and every pair of sentences σ, G in Fm: if (1) for every sentence φ and every sentence ψ, 𝓢 proves the biconditional D(φ ⇒ ψ) ⇔ (D(φ) ∧ (T(φ) ⇒ D(ψ))), (2) 𝓢 proves D(σ), and (3) 𝓢 proves D(G), then 𝓢 proves D(σ ⇒ G). The biconditional, conjunction and implications within the displayed sentences are connectives of Fm; the outer if–then is a rule about provability. Neither consistency of 𝓢 nor a proof of σ, G or T(σ) is required."}
translation: Target is defined to be the following proposition. For every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of implication, conjunction, disjunction, negation, truth and falsehood on Fm, every provability relation for S on Fm, every system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens, every pair of functions T, D from Fm to Fm, and every pair of sentences σ, G in Fm: if (1) for every sentence φ and every sentence ψ, 𝓢 proves the biconditional D(φ ⇒ ψ) ⇔ (D(φ) ∧ (T(φ) ⇒ D(ψ))), (2) 𝓢 proves D(σ), and (3) 𝓢 proves D(G), then 𝓢 proves D(σ ⇒ G). The biconditional, conjunction and implications within the displayed sentences are connectives of Fm; the outer if–then is a rule about provability. Neither consistency of 𝓢 nor a proof of σ, G or T(σ) is required.

divergences.description: The TARGET states a rule for any classical system and any sentences σ and G. It does not identify them with DTK, K =PA F, and G(F+); the determinateness results for those particular sentences enter as premises.
Def11 requires the system to prove each sentence instance of D4. It does not express the source’s single internally quantified axiom over codes: the type Fm takes the place of the Sent guards.

judgement.summary: Within the declared abstraction, the inference is exact: the relevant D4 instance and proofs of D(σ) and D(G) suffice for a proof of D(σ → G), without a proof of T(σ).
